q1_issues.issue: "further" is predicated of the group symbol as (Member sk_estimate_1 further), which the plural rules explicitly bar — a member-level property must go through the distributive rule or the kind, never onto the group symbol.

Both rankings hang off one symbol on one scale — (Ordinal sk_thing_1 4 common) and (Ordinal sk_thing_1 8 common) — so the parse asserts a single entity is simultaneously rank 4 and rank 8, and the men/women restriction is lost because the sibling In atoms bind neither ordinal.
The parse treats "show" as an attitude verb (it seals the complement under Theme) but gives its subject Agent, where the propositional-attitude section fixes Experiencer for the holder.

Statements 6-11 re-emit the sealed proposition as top-level facts, i.e. the factive dual-emit, which presumes "show" is factive — a classification the instruction set's factive/non-factive lists never make.
"Further estimates" is an indefinite bare plural, which the instruction set routes to a generic rule (verbal) or the kind, not to a definite-plural group witness.

q2_gaps: evidential "show / indicate / suggest that P" — not listed among either the factive or the non-factive attitude verbs, so whether P is asserted at top level is undetermined
a superlative/ordinal ranking restricted to a subpopulation ("the fourth most common cause of cancer in men") — Ordinal takes only entity, rank and scale, with no slot for the comparison domain
an indefinite bare-plural subject in an episodic, non-generic clause ("Further estimates show that P") — neither the generic-rule route nor the definite-plural group route fits
gapped ellipsis in a coordinated ranking ("and the eighth most common in women", with "cause of cancer" elided)
notes: The Ordinal/In scoping collapse is the substantive defect: the two rankings are mutually contradictory as flat same-scale atoms on one symbol. Of and In are otherwise used within licence (nominalization object, framing/domain oblique).
